The goal of this project is to predict an individual's Pulse using the NHANES
training data. This notebook documents the analysis of demographic, health, and lifestyle
variables associated with resting pulse rate.

## 1. Load the training data

The training data are stored in the repository `data/` directory.
```{r}
nhanes <- read.csv("data/NHANES-training.csv")
```

Check the number of rows and columns in the imported data:

```{r}
dim(nhanes)
```

## 2. Checking Variables

I first checked candidate predictors for missingness and variability, then examined their relationships with Pulse. The initial summaries below document screening before the exclusions.

```{r}
variables <- c(
  "Pulse",
  "Gender", "Age", "Race1", "Education", "MaritalStatus",
  "HHIncome", "Poverty", "Work",
  "BMI", "BPSysAve", "BPDiaAve", "Testosterone", "DirectChol", "TotChol",
  "Diabetes", "HealthGen", "DaysPhysHlthBad", "DaysMentHlthBad",
  "SleepHrsNight", "SleepTrouble",
  "PhysActive", "PhysActiveDays", "TVHrsDay", "CompHrsDay",
  "Alcohol12PlusYr", "AlcoholDay", "AlcoholYear", "Smoke100", "SmokeNow"
)
```

Check the percentage of missing values.
```{r}
round(colMeans(is.na(nhanes[variables])) * 100, 1)
```


Check the numerical variables for their ranges, unusual values, and variability.
```{r}
numerical <- c(
  "Pulse", "Age", "Poverty", "BMI", "BPSysAve", "BPDiaAve",
  "Testosterone", "DirectChol", "TotChol", "DaysPhysHlthBad",
  "DaysMentHlthBad", "SleepHrsNight", "PhysActiveDays",
  "AlcoholDay", "AlcoholYear"
)

summary(nhanes[numerical])
```

I excluded PhysActiveDays and AlcoholDay from the initial predictor list because they were missing 52.7% and 33.3% of their values, respectively. I retained PhysActive as a more complete measure of physical activity. I considered Alcohol12PlusYr and AlcoholYear as alternative alcohol measures. Rather than exclude smoking information, I combined Smoke100 and SmokeNow.

```{r}
nhanes$SmokeStatus <- ifelse(
  nhanes$Smoke100 == "No", "Under100",
  ifelse(nhanes$SmokeNow == "Yes", "Current", "Former")
)

table(nhanes$SmokeStatus)
```
Here, Under100 means fewer than 100 lifetime cigarettes. Current and Former refer to participants who reported smoking at least 100 lifetime cigarettes.

SmokeStatus replaces the two original smoking variables in subsequent EDA.



Count observations in each category of the categorical variables.
```{r}
categorical <- c(
  "Gender", "Race1", "Education", "MaritalStatus", "HHIncome",
  "Work", "Diabetes", "HealthGen", "SleepTrouble", "PhysActive",
  "TVHrsDay", "CompHrsDay", "Alcohol12PlusYr", "SmokeStatus"
)

lapply(nhanes[categorical], table, useNA = "ifany")
```
